name: Boldy James
notes: The Detroit end of the drumless lane, and the parameter the research actually singles out is silence: "deliberate use of silence between phrases" and "monotone 24–32 bar verses". Silence is authored twice over — `transitions.dropOutBeats` at 0.5 probability for four beats, the longest drop in this batch, and `melody.densityPerBar` 1–3 with `octaveJumpProb` 0.03, so the phrase that returns is the same phrase. "Loops chosen for texture over harmony; often a single chord for a whole track" is `impliedByRiff` with `chordDurationBeats` reaching 32 and a voicing register spanning 34–76. The kit is the softest-but-one here: `velocityTiers` at 78–94 / 52–64 / 26–36, `kick.densityPerBar` 1–2 at `syncopation` 0.08 for a kick that is barely there, and a hat stream at the 0.29 floor. The bass sits lowest in the batch, 20–38, because the research says "low-end movement almost nil" and the record's weight is register rather than motion. ⚠ `confidence` is medium: the research rates it medium-high, but the citation is a scene analysis that names him rather than a session that measured him. ⚠ The `i–VII` and `i–iv` families at weights 2 and 1 are **INFERRED** — the research says static `i` and nothing more — and so are every velocity tier and hat density here. ⚠ **The bass pool was widened after `bass.rs` measured it at 0.376 distinct against a floor of 0.95.** It was authored with NO passing tones, followRootsProb 0.92, anticipationProb 0.04 over register [20,38] — a faithful description of a sample-loop bass, and one that leaves a seed nothing to vary but root and octave. Now ["P5","m7"], root lock 0.84, anticipation 0.26, register [20,44]. The line is still overwhelmingly root-on-kick; what changed is how many different records it can be, not how busy any one of them is. ⚠ The chord voicing moved up to [45, 87] so the bass stays under the harmony — it started at 34 against a bass reaching 44, an overlap of 11. The span is preserved; a voicing that low was competing with the bass rather than sitting over it. ⚠ **The countermelody reached only 876 distinct answers in 1000 seeds against a floor of 980**, so it was given range: styles 3, densityRatio 0.5, melody density [1,5]. A counter is combinatorial in the styles it may pick, its density against the melody, and the phrase length it answers inside — one style over a thin density inside a single phrase length has almost nothing a seed can vary.
